_README: Operating decisions the relation definition cannot make. Feed to
Fields marked TODO are blocked on a decision, a second operator, a build, or storage.
The ceremonyId here is a UUID and is deliberately NOT the definition's ceremonyId,
which is a human-readable label; the protocol requires a UUID.

operationalPolicy._note: Owner decisions (2026-10-23, 2026-10-25): the root key may authorize website releases, CLI releases and heartbeat grace changes (30-600 s) after opening, each as a signed, publicly listed operational update. A CLI release update adds a build; earlier builds stay authorized.

primaryPublication._note: Owner decision (2026-10-23): no independent witness. Each accepted head's evidence bundle and coordinator-signed checkpoint go to this Object-Locked archive before the next lease.

schedule._TODO: Decide. Everything downstream — the beacon block, the challenge window — hangs off these.

beacon._note: Production decision: exponent 10 uses 1,024 sequential hashes, without a meaningful proposer-grinding delay. Seal before the precommitted beacon block; soundness still requires an honest ordinary contributor. Existing signed rehearsal manifests retain exponent 32.
beacon._TODO: blockNumber: a mainnet block comfortably after sealsAt (~12s/block, so 7 days is ~50,400 blocks). expectedAt: its projected time.

genesisBellman._note: Owner decision (2026-10-23): contributions use the Bellman format (bellman-transition-v1). This is the deterministic snarkjs 0.7.6 Bellman export of the pinned genesis zkey f23c5dad…; the rehearsal used the same genesis and every verifier reproduces the export at startup.

artifactUrls._note: Mainnet archive (stack moss-phase2-mainnet), copied 2026-10-25 server side from the rehearsal archive and checked against the pinned hashes. The ptau entry is load-bearing: no public source exists, so this archive is the only way anyone verifies the ceremony from the root.

coordinatorKeys._TODO: Generate: openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out secrets/coordinator-1.key && openssl pkey -in secrets/coordinator-1.key -pubout -out secrets/coordinator-1.pub. Exactly one per epoch, frozen before opening.

verifierKeys._note: Owner decision (2026-10-22): one internal verifier operator, as in the rehearsal.
verifierKeys._TODO: Generate the verifier key and record the digest of the image it will run.

contributionPolicy._note: maximumContributions is derived from targetContributions; the validator requires them equal. Owner decision (2026-10-23): 100,000 is a ceiling that is not expected to bind, so the signed seal time ends contributions. maxArtifactByteLength leaves room for 100,000 contributions in either artifact format (zkey: 567,402,188 + 435 bytes each).

webRelease._note: sha256/byteLength of web-release.json: a deterministic manifest of every asset the build serves, from `pnpm web:release --describe apps/ceremony/.next --out web-release.json` on the release commit. The browser cannot attest to its own code, so this is verified out of band: anyone runs `pnpm web:release --check <site> --manifest web-release.json`. The build is reproducible (build ID pinned to the commit) and pages carry SRI.
webRelease._TODO: Blocked on building the release commit, publishing web-release.json at an immutable URL, and a pushed sourceCommit.

cliReleases._note: Owner decision (2026-10-24): the CLI contributes in this Bellman ceremony. sha256/byteLength are of packages/cli/dist/index.js, the file the CLI hashes at run time (packages/cli/src/release.ts), built with `pnpm --filter @moss/phase2-ceremony-cli build`; this value is from the commit that pins the contribution worker and is a placeholder until the release commit. Signed operational updates can authorize later CLI builds (operationalPolicy.allowCliReleaseUpdates), so a CLI fix after signing goes out as an update.
